newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper called to open slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper called to open slightly higher.

text.p: COMEX copper futures were called to open slightly higher Monday, with LME three-month copper up but below morning highs.
COMEX March copper was called unchanged to 0.20 cent firmer from Friday's close of 103.75 cents a lb. It traded from 102.90 to 103.95 cents on ACCESS.
COMEX warehouse copper stocks fell 790 short tons to 18,971 short tons Friday. LME copper stocks jumped 26,100 tonnes Friday to 191,750 tonnes.
But the prompt market is seen remaining tight, though backwardations eased late last week.

The LME cash-to-three month spread was around $205.00 a tonne midday Monday, well off the highs at $331.00 on January 28, while the COMEX March/May spread ended Friday around 3.25 cents a pound, down from 3.85 cents on January 23.

Shorts on the LME, which are believed to include a Far East trade house, are likely to remain under pressure, because longs, including a large European trade house, are seeking to take delivery, traders said.
The focus this week though was likely to be on the introduction of LME traded average price options (TAPOS) Monday, and the LME February options declarations Wednesday, traders said.
